title: Hall Chicken Noodle Soup
seoTitle: Hall Chicken Noodle Soup | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Classic chicken noodle soup with egg noodles for ten
subtitle: Classic chicken noodle soup with egg noodles for ten
description: Chicken thighs simmer with mirepoix and herbs until tender, then shred into a rich broth with egg noodles and carrots. Simple, restorative, and built for the biggest stock pot in the hall.

steps.title: Poach the chicken
steps.instruction: Simmer chicken thighs in broth with onion, bay leaves, and thyme 30–35 minutes until internal temp reaches 165°F and meat pulls easily from bone. Target oven/smoker temperature: 165°F.

steps.title: Shred and strain
steps.instruction: Remove chicken, shred meat, discard skin and bones. Strain broth if cloudy, return to pot, and skim excess fat.

steps.title: Build the soup base
steps.instruction: Add carrots, celery, and garlic to broth. Simmer 15 minutes until vegetables tender.

steps.title: Cook noodles separately
steps.instruction: Boil egg noodles in salted water until al dente, about 7 minutes. Drain and toss with a little oil.

steps.title: Ladle and garnish
steps.instruction: Return shredded chicken to soup. Season with salt and pepper. Portion noodles into bowls, ladle hot soup over, and garnish with parsley.

proTips: A splash of lemon juice at service brightens heavy broth instantly.
Turmeric pinch adds golden color without changing the classic flavor.
Freeze half the shredded chicken and broth base separately for fast future soup.
tonightSpread: Soup with saltine crackers and buttered bread on the side.
Simple green salad for crew who want crunch alongside the bowl.
leftovers: Store noodles separate from broth or they absorb everything overnight.
Reduce broth and add cream for a quick chicken pot pie filling.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Chicken noodle soup is the universal reset meal. It reheats perfectly, fills the hall with comfort smell, and nobody complains when they are tired or under the weather.
mealPrepNotes: Poach thighs gently—boiling toughens meat. Cook noodles separately and add at service so they do not bloat in the pot. Skim fat from broth for cleaner flavor.
